title: Proper conflict-free 7-coloring of planar graphs
summary: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every nonisolated vertex has a color occurring uniquely in its open neighborhood. We prove that every graph with neither a $K_5$-minor nor a $Q_6$-minor admits such a coloring with at most seven colors, where $Q_6=K_3\vee\overline{K_3}$. In particular, this improves the previous general upper bound of eight for planar graphs. The proof combines a previously developed iterated distance-three selector construction with a general anchor-contraction lifting principle.
